title: Agent policy
description: The L1 operator policy (agent-policy.yaml): autonomy tier per machine profile, what is never read, never done, asked about, or pre-approved, network egress, and run ceilings. Engine-neutral; compiled per engine by the adapters (adapters/*/README.md). Walls are denies (forbid, deny_read); ask is a human checkpoint and protects nothing unattended (ADR-0021).

profiles.description: Machine profile name (the dotfiles' .profile) -> its autonomy tier.

deny_read.description: Path globs no agent may read (secrets, credentials). A wall: compiled to a deny on every engine or the compile fails.

forbid.description: Walls: actions denied in every mode, on every profile.

ask.description: Human checkpoints: prompt a person at a terminal. Unattended they are denials; never count them as protection.

allow.description: Pre-approvals: run without asking. Never loosens a forbid or deny_read (deny wins on every engine).

fail_if_unavailable.description: Refuse to run rather than run unsandboxed.

writable_roots.description: Directories beyond the workspace that sandboxed commands may write.

budgets.description: Run ceilings by tier. An unattended tier must have one.

accept_gaps.description: Degradations the operator accepts on purpose: an engine that cannot represent a field. Without an entry the compiler fails closed.

allOf.description: Some profile is unattended -> budgets.unattended is required (an unattended run has a ceiling).

tier.description: How often an agent asks. read-only: never writes. ask: asks before edits and commands. auto-edit: edits in the workspace without asking, asks for commands. autonomous: does not ask, walls hold (interactive operator present). unattended: headless, never asks, asks become denials, the allowlist is the boundary.

engines.description: Engines installed on this profile; the compiler emits only these.

pathGlob.description: A path glob: relative to each workspace root (**/.env), home-relative (~/.ssh/**) or absolute (//etc/** is not used; write /etc/**).

domain.description: A host, *.host for subdomains only, or **.host for the apex and subdomains.

argvToken.description: One literal argv token, or alternatives at that position.

rule.description: Exactly one matcher: command (an argv prefix, matched token by token), write (a path glob for file writes and edits), or tool (an abstract tool).

domain.description: With tool: web-fetch only, the domain the rule covers.

examples.description: Commands the rule must match; compiled to Codex match = [...] and checked by tests.
